dek: A Baltimore pick seller that says it started with the 1992 football season. Its Lock Club costs $500 a week, $1500 a month or $5000 a season per sport. Sales run through advisors on the phone, the terms say all services are non refundable unless a receipt says otherwise, and every record we saw is a run chosen by the seller.

short_answer: ATS Consultants is a real, long running pick seller. Its current site, atsbas.com, gives a Baltimore street address, toll free and international phone numbers, written terms under Maryland law, and published prices. Press releases from 2009 and 2012 show the same firm and the same 800 number. In that narrow sense the business is legitimate.

Whether the picks make money is a separate question that nothing we opened answers. The Proven Results page is a list of hot runs such as "Football Lock Club is now on a 6-1 run" and "WON 20 out of 24 weeks last season," chosen by the seller. We found no full, time stamped log of every pick with odds.

Treat ATS Consultants as an expensive seller with marketing records, not a proven winner. A $5000 season costs as much as many bettors' whole bankroll, the terms make most packages non refundable and non cancellable, and in 2012 the firm publicly apologized for promoting wins with ticket images that showed projections, not real payouts.

guarantee: The Lock Club page makes no guarantee. The Financial Program page says it is "Backed by a full money-back guarantee," but we found no written rules for that guarantee on the page: no grading period, no unit count, no claim process.

The site terms are strict. They say "all ATS Services are non-refundable unless explicitly specified otherwise on receipt," that a package "is non-cancellable under any circumstances," and that a money back guarantee is valid only where it is explicitly mentioned in writing. They also say no assurance can be given of winning or profiting. A buyer should get any guarantee written on the receipt before paying. Betting losses are never covered.

claims_note: The experience claim shifts from page to page: 34 years on the About headline and the Lock Club page, 33 years in the About stat block. Small, but the copy is not kept consistent.

The win rate claims have moved a lot over time. In 2009 the firm claimed over 66% for a football season, in 2014 a staff member said clients were on the right side 90% of the time, and the 2026 site talks in weekly runs and units without any overall rate.
"Units" are never defined on the Proven Results page, and the dollar figures assume a $250 unit. Every run on that page starts and ends where the seller chose.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that we could find. We found no full, time stamped log of every ATS pick with the line, the odds and the release time, and no third party tracking of the service.

What the seller publishes: the Proven Results page lists weekly highlights by sport, some with teams, lines and scores, and the homepage links a weekly review PDF. These are selected examples. Most picks show a spread or total with no price, and tags such as "(ffp)" and "(el)" are not explained.

One public record about the firm's marketing does exist. On 2 Jul 2012 ATS issued a press release apologizing for images of winning tickets, tied to a large preseason bet on the Miami Heat and other wagers, used to promote recent wins. The company president said the amounts shown were a projection of what clients won, that the firm never planned to cash the tickets, and "We overstepped on this, and take full responsibility for it."

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no ATS Consultants pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how ATS Consultants performs.
our_data.context: For scale: the 2009 release claimed over 66% winners and a 2014 interview claimed 90%. On the Watchdog board on 16 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard odds of 110 to win 100 a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on ATS Consultants is close to nonexistent. Almost everything online about the firm was written by the firm. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found no independent buyer reviews of ATS Consultants, positive or negative. What exists is the firm's own material across many years: 2009 press releases and free pick posts that end with a phone number to enroll, a 2014 interview, a 2012 apology for misleading ticket images, and the current atsbas.com results page. On TheRX the firm appears only on a moderator list of services whose write ups members may not post. With no buyer posts there is no pattern to report either way.

The atsbas.com Proven Results page says ATS has won nearly 40 weeks over the last two years and that Lock Club clients went on a 60 unit run last year. These are the seller's own selected results, not buyer reports.

Free ATS picks were republished on Bleacher Report in 2009 under a Touthouse byline. Each post gave one free play and closed with a call to an ATS account executive to enroll in a full season program. This shows how the firm sold, not how buyers fared.
In TheRX daily service play thread, the moderator's opening post lists ATS Consultants among services whose write ups must not be posted. No ATS plays or buyer comments appeared in that thread.

A Better Business Bureau search for ATS Consultants in Baltimore returned no results. Our web searches found no Sportsbook Review, Covers or TheRX thread in which a buyer described results with ATS, and no court or regulator action naming the firm.

conflicts: ATS sells by phone through account executives and advisors. A sales call is where buyers get pitched bigger packages, so decide your budget before you call.
The 2012 apology shows the firm once advertised client wins with ticket images that, by its own account, were projections. Weigh the current results page with that history in mind.
strengths: A named firm with a Baltimore street address, two phone numbers, an email and written terms under Maryland law.
Prices for every Lock Club and Financial Program package are published on the site.
The firm has used the same name and 800 number since at least 2009, and it publicly owned up to a misleading 2012 promotion.
concerns: No full public record. Every number we saw is a run or total chosen by the seller.
The Lock Club is expensive: $500 for one week or $5000 for one season of one sport.
The terms make services non refundable unless the receipt says otherwise and packages non cancellable, while the Financial Program page advertises a full money back guarantee with no written rules.
Win rate claims have ranged from over 66% in 2009 to 90% in 2014, far above what verified long run bettors achieve.
No independent buyer reviews to weigh, good or bad.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Get any guarantee written on the receipt. These terms only honor one that is explicit in writing.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is a real firm with a Baltimore address, phone numbers, written terms and published prices, active under the same name since at least 2009. We could not verify that its picks win over time, because it publishes no full record, and we found no independent buyer reviews.
How much does ATS Consultants cost?
On 16 Nov 2026 the Lock Club cost $500 a week, $1500 a month or $5000 a full season per sport, and the Financial Program cost $75 a week, $199 a month or $599 a season per sport.

The terms say services are non refundable unless the receipt explicitly says otherwise, and packages cannot be cancelled. The Financial Program page advertises a money back guarantee, so get its terms in writing before paying.

For the money you get the plays released in the period you buy and access to phone advisors. What is unproven is whether the picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at standard odds over hundreds of plays, and at $5000 a season the price alone takes a large bankroll to recover.
